note:
THE PROSE-ONLY FLOOR IS ~657 s, MEASURED TWICE, AND THE CLOSE SEQUENCE PAYS IT PER FINDING.

Two observations minutes apart, both campaign/the-pavement, both docs-only, both admitted prose-only by sluice_is_prose_only itself (I called the function, I did not eyeball the paths):

  5b4b0c1e805d   2 files  +67 lines   655 s
  f6b2f8cfd620   2 files  +~63 lines  659 s

4 s apart. That is a floor, not noise. The skip IS working — the same campaign's real merge was 1773 s, so it saves ~63% — but the irreducible cost of landing sixty lines of prose through the queue is eleven minutes of the one serial resource every other campaign waits behind.

THE SEQUENCING THAT MAKES IT RECUR, WHICH IS STRUCTURAL AND NOT ANYONE'S SLOPPINESS. The Pavement landed three times in two hours:

  7f2599f76   the campaign itself                        1773 s
  5b4b0c1e8   its own parked findings, before teardown    655 s
  f6b2f8cfd   two findings Nathan raised AT CLOSE         659 s

~1314 s — about 42% of the campaign's total box time — spent landing ~130 lines of documentation that all belong to the same close.

Neither follow-up was avoidable by trying harder. campaign-autopilot makes G6 a HARD STOP where Nathan reviews at merge; submitting-to-the-sluice makes a merge THE LAST ACT of a campaign. Both are correct on their own and together they guarantee that review findings arrive after the artifact they would have changed was already submitted. The second landing has an additional forcing function: the Cartulary discipline says promote findings out of scratch BEFORE teardown, because .superpowers/sdd/ dies with the worktree — so a campaign that has closed still has durable writing left to do.

WHAT I AM NOT PROPOSING. Not 'batch your closes' — you cannot batch input you have not received. Not lowering the floor as the primary fix; 657 s for a two-file docs merge is worth understanding but the merge, worktree setup and unskipped phases are most of it, and shaving it does not change the shape. Not a rule change of any kind: this touches the campaign process, not the queue, and it is not the operator's call.

THE SHAPE, STATED PLAINLY SO SOMEONE CAN DECIDE ABOUT IT: a campaign worktree must stay alive past its own merge to absorb review, and nothing in the process says so. The Cartulary's warning points the other way — scratch dies with the worktree — which is exactly the pressure that produced landing #2 here.

Recorded because three green rows look unremarkable in sluice-status and this cost is invisible in them. Every one of the three was correctly submitted, correctly vetted, and correctly landed. The cost is in the seam between two skills that are each right.
